newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed securities yawn after FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed securities yawn after FOMC meeting.

text.p: Mortgage-backed security prices were mostly lower late Tuesday, with discount mortgage coupons 2/32 lower to 1/32 firmer and premium coupons 2/32 lower to 1/32 higher.

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) did little to affect prices when Fed policy makers decided to hold rates steady. Treasuries saw little activity after the FOMC meeting adjourned, and players said mortgage-backed prices mirrored this apathy.
"The FOMC decision was as expected," said a New York MBS trader.

Government National Mortgage Association 7.5 perecent mortgage securities were off 1/32 late Tuesday at 101 8/32 to yield 7.338 percent. Fannie Mae 7.5 percent securities were down 2/32 at 101 7/32, while Freddie Mac 7.5 percent securities were down 2/32 at 101 13/32.

A New York trader said Tuesday's session "has been one of the quietest for a while" and suggested the activity would remain subdued until after Labor Day when many traders return from summer vacations.
The 10-year Treasury note, meanwhile, remained unchanged at 99 12/32 to yield 6.21 percent.
Prior to the FOMC meeting, participants said, mortgage securites were directionless and were little affected by July housing states data.

As reported, July housing starts were flat at an annual rate oif 1.447 million units. Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a slight increase. "People didn't seem to care even thoughit was a little bullish for Treasuries," said the New York trader.
One market observer said investors would watch upcoming economic data to discern any inflationary currents in the nation's economy.

"There is uncertainty among investors where Treasuries are going," said one market watcher. He added that U.S. government securities would probably be range bound over the next two weeks because many investors were waiting to see the August employment report to be released the first week of September.

The New York pass-through trader noted that some market players may be mulling the creation of collateralized mortgage obligations (CMOs). The New York MBS salesman agreed: "7.5 percent coupons are a little less than a basis point tighter which means people may think about the origination of a CMO."

The salesman conceded that investor demand for CMO product will be an important determinant in the creation of CMOs. And, he noted, the key to CMO creation is a steep Treasury yield curve. The curve steepened in the wake of the Friday's stock market sell-off but has since flattened as these losses were erased.
A CMO is a multiclass bond backed by a pool of mortgage pass-through securities or mortgage loans.
